title: Models and the Foundry catalog · Level 3
slo: Describe language models and use the Foundry catalog to find suitable models.

options.text: An environment for generative AI models
options.rationale: This is correct. Foundry supports discovering, evaluating, deploying, and operating generative models.

options.error_type: Confuses the platform with a model
options.rationale: Foundry contains a catalog and deployment options for many models. It is not one model.
options.better_fit: Choose a single model when you need response generation for an application.

feedback.intrinsic: This would mistake the work environment for one of the models used within it.
feedback.instructional: Foundry brings together capabilities for working with many generative models.

options.error_type: Confuses the platform with an evaluation result
options.rationale: Comparison scores help evaluate models. Foundry is the integrated environment where evaluation can occur.
options.better_fit: Use a comparison score when judging model performance.

feedback.intrinsic: A score would not provide the broader workspace for model work.
feedback.instructional: Foundry is an environment; benchmark and comparison results are pieces of evaluation information.

options.error_type: Confuses the platform with a testing feature
options.rationale: Playground settings configure how a deployed model responds. Foundry includes the playground but is broader than it.
options.better_fit: Use playground settings when testing prompts and response behavior.

feedback.intrinsic: This would reduce the full environment to one testing feature.
feedback.instructional: Foundry includes discovery, evaluation, deployment, and operation, not just playground settings.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Foundry is an integrated environment for the model lifecycle.

exercises.question_text: What can a Foundry model entry include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. A model entry can include benchmark results and performance comparisons.
This is correct. Model entries can list supported fine-tuning options.
This is correct. Entries can include model cards, constraints, and caveats.

options.error_type: Confuses model entry details with an agent capability
options.rationale: An agent can break goals into structured steps and execute workflows. A model entry lists information about the model instead.
options.better_fit: Use an agent when a reusable component must carry out a workflow.

feedback.intrinsic: This would look for a completed worker process where model details should be reviewed.
feedback.instructional: Model entries provide capabilities, benchmarks, tasks, fine-tuning options, and responsible-use documentation.

exercises.explanation: Correct! These details help compare a model's fit, performance, and constraints.

exercises.question_text: Language models are built on top of agents.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This reverses the relationship between the two.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Language models provide the basis, while agents package a model with instructions and optional actions.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The relationship goes in the other direction: agents are built with models.

exercises.question_text: You can use Microsoft Foundry without an Azure subscription.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The setup would be missing a required starting condition.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use of Foundry requires an Azure subscription, then a Foundry project is created to begin.

exercises.explanation: Correct! An Azure subscription is required to use Foundry.

exercises.question_text: An ___ is the work a model performs when generating or processing output.

parts.text: is the work a model performs when generating or processing output.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would describe measurement, customization, documentation, or scoring rather than output-related work.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use inference task for the work a model performs when generating or processing output. A benchmark result compares performance, fine-tuning adapts a model, model cards document it, and evaluators score outputs.

exercises.explanation: An inference task describes the work performed when a model generates or processes output. Benchmarks, fine-tuning, model cards, and evaluators describe different kinds of information or activities.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The description of the model capability becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with language models, then state their response-generating capability and its generative-AI context.

exercises.correct_answer: Language models generate varied responses for generative AI solutions
exercises.explanation: This sentence focuses on the response variety that language models can support in generative AI solutions.

exercises.question_text: Models sold directly by Azure provide enterprise service level agreements, also called ___.

parts.text: Models sold directly by Azure provide enterprise service level agreements, also called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The chosen term would refer to model size, documentation, or customization instead of a service agreement.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use SLA for service level agreement. LLM and SLM name model types, model cards are documentation, and fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model.

exercises.explanation: SLA means service level agreement. Enterprise-grade SLAs are one benefit of models sold directly by Azure.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the government workload first, then connect it to the possible need for a domain-specialized model.

exercises.correct_answer: Government workloads may require a domain-specialized model instead
exercises.explanation: This sentence distinguishes specialized government workloads from lightweight phone-app use cases. Such workloads may need a domain-specialized model.

exercises.question_text: Which filters can you use in the Foundry model catalog? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. The catalog can filter models by source.
This is correct. Capabilities are one available catalog filter.
This is correct. The catalog can filter by inference tasks.

options.error_type: Confuses catalog filtering with an agent capability
options.rationale: Working memory is something agents can maintain during a conversation. It is not listed as a catalog filter.
options.better_fit: Consider working memory when describing what an agent can do in a conversation.

feedback.intrinsic: This would search for an agent behavior instead of narrowing model choices.
feedback.instructional: Catalog filters include source, capabilities, and inference tasks; working memory belongs to agents.

exercises.explanation: Correct! These filters help narrow a large set of model choices.

exercises.question_text: A research lead needs rapid experimentation with an open-source model for a specialized task. Which model source is the best fit?

options.rationale: This is correct. These models include open-source or vendor-hosted choices and support experimentation and specialized tasks.

options.error_type: Confuses enterprise Azure hosting with open-source experimentation
options.rationale: Azure-direct models focus on Microsoft hosting, strong Azure integration, SLAs, security, and compliance. The scenario instead calls for open-source experimentation.
options.better_fit: Choose Azure-direct models when their enterprise Azure features are the priority.

feedback.intrinsic: The research lead could overlook the source type suited to open-source experimentation.
feedback.instructional: Partner and community models are the catalog source associated with open-source choices and rapid innovation.

options.error_type: Confuses general pretrained capability with the model source choice
options.rationale: Foundation models are broad pretrained models that provide general capabilities. This does not identify the source suited to open-source experimentation.
options.better_fit: Use foundation model when describing a pretrained base layer for applications.

feedback.intrinsic: The lead would have a category label but not the needed source choice.
feedback.instructional: The scenario asks about provider and hosting source. Partner and community models fit that need.

options.error_type: Confuses task specialization with provider and hosting source
options.rationale: A specialized task may affect model selection, but this label does not establish an open-source source. Partner and community models include models suitable for specialized tasks.
options.better_fit: Use a domain-specific model when an industry-specific application needs it.

feedback.intrinsic: The lead could focus only on specialization and miss the open-source requirement.
feedback.instructional: Consider both needs: partner and community models support open-source experimentation and specialized work.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Partner and community models are the best match for open-source experimentation on a specialized task.

exercises.question_text: The Foundry model catalog is a central hub for models from many providers.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would overlook why the catalog is useful for comparing choices.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The catalog is a central hub for discovering and using models from an extensive range of providers.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The catalog brings together a wide selection of models from many providers.

exercises.question_text: A government service lead is selecting AI for a specialized public-service workload. Which considerations best support the choice? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. A government application may require a domain-specialized model.

options.text: Match the model to the workload.
options.rationale: This is correct. Different workloads can require different model types.

options.text: Choose an SLM because it suits phone apps.
options.error_type: Confuses the lightweight phone-app use case with a specialized government workload
options.rationale: An SLM may suit a lightweight phone app. That does not make it the stated choice for specialized government work.
options.better_fit: Consider an SLM when a lightweight phone application is the workload.

feedback.intrinsic: The service could select based on an unrelated mobile-app situation.
feedback.instructional: Choose based on the actual workload. Specialized government work may need a domain-specialized model.

options.text: Use a foundation-model label as the selection rule.
options.error_type: Confuses a model category with a workload-based decision
options.rationale: A foundation model is a broad pretrained model category. The selection should still consider workload and task needs.
options.better_fit: Use the foundation-model category when describing general pretrained models.

feedback.intrinsic: A broad label alone would not show whether the model fits the public-service workload.
feedback.instructional: Model categories are useful descriptions, but fit comes from matching the model to the workload.

exercises.explanation: Correct! A specialized government workload may call for a domain-specialized model, selected to fit the work.
